questions.question: State the law of conservation of energy and use it to explain the energy changes of a roller coaster, including why each hill must be lower than the first.
questions.expected_answer: Energy cannot be created or destroyed; it can only be changed from one form to another or transferred, so the total stays the same. A motor changes electrical energy into the car's gravitational potential energy at the top of the first hill; going down, potential energy changes into kinetic energy; going up the next hill, kinetic changes back into potential energy. Friction with the track and air resistance change some energy into heat and sound, which can no longer lift the car, so each later hill must be lower. The brakes change the last kinetic energy into heat.

questions.question: Describe the energy transfers within a cell phone and explain, using numbers, how the law of conservation applies to a light bulb.
questions.expected_answer: Chemical potential energy in the battery changes into electrical energy, which changes into light (screen), sound (speaker), kinetic energy (vibration), radio waves, and heat (the phone warms). For a bulb: if 100 units of electrical energy go in, the light plus heat coming out add up to 100 units, for example 10 units of light and 90 units of heat in a filament bulb; energy is not lost, only changed into less useful heat.

questions.question: Trace the energy from the Sun to a moving taxi and explain why a perpetual-motion machine is impossible.
questions.expected_answer: Sunlight's energy was captured by ancient plants as chemical potential energy; their remains formed crude oil, refined into diesel (chemical potential energy); burning diesel in the engine releases heat that pushes pistons, giving the taxi kinetic energy; braking changes kinetic energy into heat in the brakes and road. A perpetual-motion machine is impossible because energy cannot be created, so it cannot give out energy without input, and friction and air resistance always change some kinetic energy into heat, so any machine without input slows and stops.
